answerable: Long-term water balance partitioning of P into surface/subsurface runoff, ET, and recharge along the Naches elevation gradient
How elevation (rain/snow phase, energy load) controls partitioning

Coarse validation of runoff seasonality against available daily USGS stream-gauge records
not_answerable: Direct point validation of simulated ET (no flux towers in domain)
Fully distributed, gridded basin-scale routed streamflow (single-column campaign cannot resolve lateral routing to gauge outlets)

parsed.n_justification: The dominant control on partitioning in this montane basin (352-1977 m) is the elevation-driven rain/snow phase transition and energy availability, so columns are placed to span the SNOTEL-relevant elevation gradient. Five columns capture low valley (rain-dominated), rain-snow transition, seasonal-snow, and high alpine (snow-dominated) regimes; two of them are duplicated in soil texture to probe the secondary texture control without over-expanding the ensemble given sparse validation data.
requires_capabilities: GSWP3 or Daymet 1980-2018 atmospheric forcing extraction at column coordinates
Accelerated-decomposition + final spinup (AD/postAD) prior to transient run for equilibrated soil moisture and water table
SNOTEL SWE retrieval for 6 stations for snow validation
USGS NWIS well WTD and stream-gauge daily-value retrieval for validation
Water-balance closure diagnostics (P = ET + runoff + recharge + dStorage)
PFLOTRAN coupling (optional) for higher-fidelity vadose-zone recharge estimation
assumptions: Recharge is approximated by ELM QCHARGE (flux to unconfined aquifer) plus QDRAI, since ELM has no explicit deep-aquifer module by default
Single-column runs represent local vertical water balance; lateral routing/discharge to specific gauges is not simulated, so gauge validation is limited to seasonality and timing
ET validation is indirect (via energy/snow/soil-moisture consistency) given no flux towers
Column soil textures are assigned from SSURGO/gridded soil data at each elevation band and used to test the secondary texture control
A ~200-year AD spinup + 100-year postAD spinup cycling 1980-2018 forcing achieves hydrologic equilibrium before the 1980-2018 transient analysis period
First 5-10 transient years are treated as additional equilibration and excluded from long-term partitioning statistics
Vegetation is prescribed from satellite land-cover (evergreen needleleaf forest at mid/low, shrub/grass at alpine) using a satellite-phenology (SP) configuration unless BGC is required
